lesson.menu_desc: Phase 4 -- tell the story of a trip from the point of view of what was done, with advanced passive constructions -- 34 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 35 -- The Trip Was Organized By... -- Advanced Passive
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Mark Kazuyoshi Seki Omagari | Lesson 35 -- The Trip Was Organized By...
lesson.grammar_point: advanced passive constructions (continuous passive with being, perfect passive with been, modal passive, passive infinitive and gerund, and the get-passive)

listenings.text: Hi Mark. Last class you compared two cities and said exactly how much of everything each one had. Today you tell the story of a trip, but from a different angle. A trip is a hundred things that somebody does for you, and most of the time nobody cares who did them. When the thing matters more than the person, English uses the passive, and the verb be changes form to tell you when it happened. If the action was in progress, use being. Our bags were being checked when the alarm went off. If it was already finished, use been. The hotel had already been booked. After a modal, like must, can or should, use be, and never to. Passports must be shown at the gate. After verbs like want, expect and need, use to be. We expected to be picked up. After hate, avoid or a preposition, use being. I hate being told to wait. And in conversation, when something unplanned happens, people often say get. My bag got lost. Now the traps. Being and been sound alike, but one is in progress and the other is finished. Never put to after a modal. And some verbs, like happen and arrive, have no passive at all. The mix-up happened, never was happened. Before class, tell the story of a trip you took, and use five of these.

Hello, this is Ken from Sakura Tours, calling with an update on your trip to Japan. First, the good news. Your flights have been confirmed, and your seats have been upgraded to the front of the plane at no extra cost. Your boarding passes will be sent by email two days before you fly. Second, the transfer. You will be picked up at Narita Airport by one of our drivers, but the time has been rescheduled for three in the afternoon, because your flight lands a little later than planned. Now, the hotel in Kyoto. I am afraid the building is being repaired this summer, so your booking has been moved to our partner hotel, which is five minutes from the station. Nothing needs to be paid for the change. Finally, two small things. Passports must be valid for the whole trip, and every bag must be labeled with your name. If anything is left on the train, it is usually handed in at the lost and found, so do not panic. Please call me back if anything needs to be changed. Thank you.

extra_audio.text: Months before the trip, the flights were booked by a tour operator, and the hotel was paid for. At the airport, we found out that our boarding passes had been printed with the wrong names. While the mix-up was being sorted out, the whole group had to wait at the desk for twenty minutes. Then my bag got stopped at the security check because of a bottle of water. In the end, everything was fixed, and we even got upgraded to a bigger room in Kyoto.
